tldr: Survey respondents across diverse backgrounds prioritize: universal Preschool for All and childcare access as workforce infrastructure; higher wages, union protections, and labor enforcement; progressive taxation (wealth, capital gains, income taxes on high earners) to fund public goods; affordable housing including public/social housing models; environmental protections especially limiting data-center incentives; and robust K-12 and higher-education funding. Some respondents call for lower business taxes and lighter regulation. One respondent critiques the Prosperity Council's composition as undemocratic and under-representative of workers and communities.

bullets.text: Preschool for All program cited repeatedly as essential public infrastructure for workforce development, with documented 3-to-1 return on investment and family income gains
Respondents call for higher minimum wages, union triggers, and enforcement of labor laws; one proposes doubling Oregon union density from ~16% to 32%
Progressive taxation proposals include wealth taxes, capital-gains taxes, and higher income-tax rates on high earners to fund childcare, education, and public housing
Multiple respondents oppose tax incentives for data centers and call for moratoria on discretionary corporate tax breaks; SB 1507 (QSBS removal) criticized for discouraging startups
K-12 and higher-education funding increases urged as critical workforce development; respondents note underfunding at PSU, SOU, PCC causing budget crises
Housing affordability identified as major barrier; proposals include public/social housing (Seattle and Maryland models cited), rent control, and infill zoning
Paid Leave Oregon and universal single-payer healthcare cited as successful worker-support models; one respondent cites Oregon's #1 Oxfam ranking on worker-friendly policy
One detailed response proposes converting Oregon economy toward worker cooperatives and democratic economic governance, citing Quebec, Colorado, and other state models
Respondent explicitly critiques Prosperity Council composition as undemocratic, citing unequal representation of workers, labor unions, and marginalized communities vs. business leaders
Environmental protection priorities include strict regulations on data-center water/energy use, protection of farmland and forests, and opposition to new refineries

programs: Oregon Main Street Community Revitalization Grant
